tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Check your VocalLab points balance and confirm your API key works. Points are billed by text length — about 15 characters per point on the API (1 point ≈ 1 second of audio).

tools.name: list_voices
tools.description: List voices you can use: the public catalog plus your own cloned and designed voices. Pass a returned `id` as the `voice` argument to generate_speech.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List the speech models you can pass as `model` to generate_speech: VocalLab Studio (v-studio, default, steerable + 200+ languages), Studio Flash (v-flash, 200+ languages, ~5x faster, 3/4 points), Pro (v-pro), and Lite (v-lite, half the points).

tools.name: generate_speech
tools.description: Convert text to speech with a VocalLab voice. Returns the generated audio inline, so you can play or save it without fetching anything — very long clips fall back to a download URL. Up to 2,000 characters per call (less on limited-access accounts; the error names the cap) — each call is one synthesi

tools.name: get_speech
tools.description: Look up a generation by id: its status and the links to download (audio_url) or directly stream (stream_url) the finished audio, plus its SRT captions link. Use the id returned by generate_speech.

tools.name: get_captions
tools.description: Get subtitles for a generation as an SRT file — timed from the actual speech, with any [emotion] markup and <break/> pauses stripped out. `phrase` mode gives readable subtitle lines; `word` mode gives one cue per word (karaoke-style highlighting). Use the id returned by generate_speech.

tools.name: design_voice
tools.description: Create brand-new voices from a written description — no recording needed. Returns up to 3 candidate previews, each with a listenable URL and a `preview_id`. Nothing is saved yet: pick the one you like and call save_designed_voice with its preview_id. Costs points (each preview is a real synthesis of

tools.name: save_designed_voice
tools.description: Keep one of the previews from design_voice as a permanent voice on the account. The returned id can be passed straight to generate_speech as `voice`. Uses one of the designed-voice slots included in the plan.

tools.name: clone_voice
tools.description: Create a voice that sounds like a specific person, from one short recording (about 30 seconds of clean speech). Almost any audio file works — MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, OGG, FLAC, WebM and more are converted server-side, and anything longer than 30 seconds is trimmed. The audio must be passed as base64, so

tools.name: list_voice_languages
tools.description: List the languages supported by clone_voice and design_voice, plus the size limits for a cloning recording. Check this before cloning — the language codes differ from the ones on the catalog voices.

tools.name: delete_voice
tools.description: Permanently delete one of your own cloned or designed voices. This cannot be undone, and any audio already generated with it is unaffected. Catalog voices can't be deleted. Use an id from list_voices.

tools.name: delete_speech
tools.description: Permanently delete a generation you own — both its stored audio file and its record. This cannot be undone. Use the id returned by generate_speech.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: clone_voice · Private data: get_balance, get_captions, clone_voice, delete_speech · Public sink: clone_voice · Destructive: delete_voice, delete_speech.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: clone_voice · Private data: get_balance, get_captions, clone_voice, delete_speech · Public sink: clone_voice · Destructive: delete_voice, delete_speech

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
